text:
Hannah: Quick question  we have a handful of late review submissions and a few manager exception requests asking to accept post-deadline edits. What's the official small-requests flow?
PeopleOpsBot: Current late submissions: 7. Exception requests: 3. Exception policy v2 available at /docs/perf/late-exceptions.md.
Eli: Are exceptions auto-denied after X hours or do we triage manually? Some are just typo fixes.
Meera: Policy summary: small edits (typos, clarity, <3 bullet examples) can be allowed with manager attestation + people-ops approval within 48h. Rating changes require HR review and calibration lead signoff.
Owen: Can we accept edits if manager signs a quick attestation saying no change to rating intent? Saves time.
Hannah: That's our current lean approach. Attestation text needs to be pasted into the form comments and include: "I attest this edit does not change the rating intent." People Ops must approve before calibration export.
Eli: How do we track these exceptions in the export so calibration leads know which rows had post-deadline edits?
Meera: We'll add two columns: exception_flag=true/false and exception_note with manager attestation text. Also exception_status: pending/approved/denied. PeopleOps will reconcile before packet publish.
Owen: If a manager changes rating post-deadline, does that automatically trigger recalibration?
Meera: Yes. Any rating change after deadline is an automatic HR review. Depending on timing, calibration leads can decide to surface the change as an update or request a quick manager summary during the session.
Hannah: Can we short-circuit on minor clarity edits? For example, swapping "led" -> "supported" in an example shouldn't need HR review.
Meera: Agreed. Minor wording changes that don't affect outcome are fine with attestation. We'll liberalize on that to avoid unnecessary overhead.
PeopleOpsBot: Template attestation added to /templates/attestations/late-edit.txt
Eli: Timeline: managers requesting exceptions should submit attestation + updated form by EOD tomorrow. People Ops will approve or deny by noon the following day.
Owen: What about managers who missed deadline because of extended customer travel and have multiple late edits? More than 3 edits — do we still treat as small?
Meera: If there are multiple substantive edits (>3 bullets or new examples added), treat as substantive  escalate to HR review. We have to preserve calibration integrity.
Hannah: Can People Ops maintain a tiny exception log so we can audit later? Columns: manager, employee_id, change_summary, attestation_text, status, approved_by, ts.
PeopleOpsBot: Exception log table created: /data/exports/exception_log_q2.csv (write-protected).
Eli: For calibration packet, please surface exception rows with a flag and link to exception_log row. That way reviewers can click for context.
Meera: Will do. Also, if a late rating change occurs within 48h of the calibration meeting, calibration lead can request a manager to present the change live (2-min summary) or defer discussion until follow-up meeting.
Owen: Good plan. For managers who will request many exceptions, can we offer a one-time 24h grace window if their director signs off? That avoids floods of small asks.
Hannah: I'm okay with a one-time, director-approved 24h grace for extenuating circumstances (travel, emergency). Must be requested before calibration packet publish.
PeopleOpsBot: Grace window request form: /forms/grace-window. Current requests: 1 pending.
Eli: Final ask  can People Ops publish a short FAQ in the playbook describing examples of allowed vs disallowed edits? Managers will appreciate clarity.
Meera: Yes, I'll draft an FAQ and sample attestation language. Will post doc link here when done.
Hannah: Thanks. I'll inform managers in my director group and ask them to use the attestation template. Closing loop for now.
PeopleOpsBot: Reminder scheduled: exception attestation deadline ping to managers in 24 hours.
